bounds: Two once-started callers, each selecting append, replacement or deletion. One exclusive lease with one token per caller; any number of modeled expirations before callers settle. One task and its listing index.

The primary task mutation and lease-token comparison are one Redis command. Listing zadd/expire/zrem remain separate operations with possible failure and lag. Index repair, pagination completeness and tenant/index migration are outside this instance.

Real implementation checks use a single loopback Redis server and explicit synchronous memory backend. Redis Cluster cross-slot support, failover, acknowledged-write durability, unknown transport outcomes, arbitrary concurrent clients, task semantic policy and downstream provider effects remain outside this proof.

Conformance executes eleven named real-store scenarios. It is not a generated-trace refinement proof. Foreign read/update/delete refusal is tested but cross-tenant noninterference across all methods is not proved.

Separate index instance covers one task ID, two organizations, attempted foreign replacement, and legal reuse after deletion with a stale original index. Listing rechecks each retained entry's organization before publication.

assumptions: Weak fairness of each active caller and lease expiry. Redis commands settle, perhaps with failure. Only two invocations are admitted, so indefinite external contention and a permanently unavailable Redis server are excluded.
Weak fairness of the separate listing-index attempt, which can succeed or fail. One global task ID can be reassigned to a second organization while its original index entry remains.
